headline: Quick Pulse Activity - 3-Minute ESL Warm-Up Poll
outcomes: Students answer fast, low-pressure prompts so the whole class speaks from the first minutes of the lesson
The teacher sees an instant distribution of opinions, confidence, or prior knowledge before choosing the next move
Short prompts lower anxiety for quiet students because everyone responds at the same time
The result screen gives the class a natural reason to compare answers and explain choices
howItWorks: LessonCaptain generates three mini-prompts connected to your topic or lesson goal
Students answer from their phones or laptops while the teacher screen tracks responses live
The class sees the response distribution after each prompt, not a long report after the activity
The teacher uses the strongest split or surprise result as the first discussion question
teacherUseCases: Opening a lesson with a quick opinion check before a reading, video, or debate
Checking background knowledge before teaching a new topic
Restarting energy after a break with a fast whole-class participation moment

faq.q: What kind of prompts does Quick Pulse generate?
faq.a: Prompts are short and easy to answer quickly: agreement checks, preference choices, confidence ratings, or prediction questions. They are designed to start conversation, not test students formally.

faq.q: Can Quick Pulse work with one student?
faq.a: Yes. With one student it becomes a fast diagnostic or conversation starter. In groups, the distribution reveal adds extra energy because students can compare how the room answered.
No. Quick Pulse is a warm-up and check-in activity. The value comes from participation and discussion, not points.

faq.q: How do students answer the pulse prompts?
faq.a: No. Students join through a browser link on any device. They do not need to install an app or create a student account.

faq.q: When should I use Quick Pulse?
faq.a: Use it when you need the class talking quickly: the first minutes of class, before a source-based lesson, before a debate, or after a long teacher explanation.
